USS Arizona. A Pennsylvania-class battleship that sank in 102 seconds during the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941, killing 1,177 of her 1,377-person crew. She became the most iconic American casualty of the attack and remains a war grave at the bottom of Pearl Harbor.

Arizona was launched in 1915 and served in the Pacific Fleet as one of America's most advanced capital ships before Pearl Harbor. During the attack, she was hit by a high-altitude bomb that penetrated her forward magazine, triggering a catastrophic explosion and fire that engulfed the ship in minutes. She lost 1,177 men, more than any other ship at Pearl Harbor, with most entombed in the wreck, making her the costliest ship loss of the entire Pacific War in terms of crew fatalities.

Left resting on the harbor bottom, her superstructure remains visible above the waterline, serving as a submarine memorial and national monument. The USS Arizona Memorial, built over her remains in 1962, has become one of America's most visited war monuments and a pilgrimage site for those honoring Pearl Harbor casualties. Her loss steeled American resolve to prosecute the Pacific War and inflict eventual victory over Japan. This Pennsylvania-class battleship was representative of the battleship-centric naval doctrine that existed before aircraft became the dominant naval weapon, and her fate remains inextricably linked to December 7, 1941, the day that will live in infamy.
